name: SpaceX
short_description: Reusable rockets with the Falcon family and the Starship program; operator of Starlink.
why_relevant: Made spaceflight cheap and routine for the entire industry.
history: Founded in 2002 by Elon Musk, SpaceX set out to slash the cost of reaching orbit. Falcon 1 reached orbit in 2008; Falcon 9 first flew in 2010 and achieved the first landing of an orbital booster in 2015. Crew Dragon began carrying NASA astronauts in 2020, and Starlink now operates thousands of satellites. Starship, the fully reusable super-heavy system, has advanced through increasingly ambitious test flights. Privately held and among the world's most valuable startups, SpaceX dominates commercial launch.

name: Blue Origin
short_description: Developer of New Glenn and the BE-4 engine for cargo and crew launch.
why_relevant: Heavy-lift reusable launcher now serving NASA and commercial customers.
history: Founded in 2000 by Jeff Bezos, Blue Origin spent years developing the New Shepard suborbital vehicle, which began carrying paying passengers in 2021. The company manufactures the BE-4 engine, selected for United Launch Alliance's Vulcan and for its own New Glenn heavy-lift rocket, which reached orbit on its debut in 2025. Backed by Bezos's personal investment, Blue Origin is now a major NASA and commercial launch supplier pursuing reusable orbital access and lunar landers.

name: Astranis
short_description: Builds dedicated micro-geostationary satellites that split a GEO slot into beams.
why_relevant: Dedicated connectivity for underserved GEO regions at a fraction of legacy cost.
history: Founded in 2015 in San Francisco, Astranis set out to shrink geostationary communications satellites to roughly a tenth of traditional size. Its first MicroGEO satellite launched in 2023, and the company has signed deals to deliver dedicated bandwidth to Alaska, the Philippines, and Latin America. After raising several hundred million dollars, Astranis manufactures small GEO spacecraft that split a single orbital slot into many spot beams for underserved regions.

name: Relativity Space
short_description: Prints its rockets with robotic wire-arc additive manufacturing.
why_relevant: Swapped thousands of rocket parts for a handful of 3D-printed ones.
history: Founded in 2015, Relativity Space pioneered large-scale 3D printing of rockets with its Stargate robotic wire-arc printers. The Terran 1 rocket launched in 2023, proving that a mostly 3D-printed vehicle could fly. The company then pivoted to the larger Terran R and later toward defense applications. Despite funding challenges and leadership changes, Relativity remains a flagship of additive manufacturing in aerospace from its Long Beach headquarters.

name: Firefly Aerospace
short_description: Operator of the Alpha rocket and Blue Ghost lunar lander.
why_relevant: First commercial lander to fully succeed on the Moon in 2025.
history: Founded in 2014, Firefly Aerospace overcame a troubled early history to fly its Alpha rocket successfully in 2023. Its Blue Ghost lunar lander achieved the first fully successful commercial Moon landing in 2025. Backed by AE Industrial Partners, Firefly develops launch vehicles and lunar landers and has won NASA contracts, positioning itself as a full-spectrum provider of small-to-medium space transportation from Cedar Park, Texas.

name: ABL Space Systems
short_description: Designed the RS1 rocket for launch from shipping containers.
why_relevant: Pushed toward extremely mobile, low-cost launch sites.
history: Founded in 2017, ABL Space Systems developed the RS1 rocket, designed to launch from standard shipping containers and enable rapid deployment from austere sites. After a 2023 launch failure from Alaska, the company faced setbacks and layoffs while continuing to refine its mobile ground systems. Based in El Segundo, ABL's containerized architecture aims to give small satellite operators flexible, low-cost access to orbit with minimal infrastructure.

name: Planet Labs
short_description: Operates the biggest fleet of Earth-imaging satellites, imaging the whole planet daily.
why_relevant: Imaged the entire Earth's land mass every day for agriculture and defense.
history: Founded in 2010 by former NASA scientists, Planet Labs deployed the largest commercial Earth-imaging constellation, its Dove cubesats. It went public via a SPAC in 2021 and now images the entire landmass daily. Pelican and SuperDove satellites improved resolution, and the data serves agriculture, defense, and climate monitoring. Headquartered in San Francisco, Planet remains the leading provider of daily global monitoring from space.

name: Spire Global
short_description: Provides weather, AIS and RF data from a global small-sat constellation.
why_relevant: Complements forecast models with dense atmospheric probe data.
history: Founded in 2012, Spire Global operates a constellation of small satellites collecting weather, maritime AIS, and aviation data using radio occultation and signals intelligence. The company went public in 2021 and sells data to governments and industry. Headquartered in San Francisco with major operations in Glasgow, Spire provides dense atmospheric measurements that improve global forecast models and tracks vessels and aircraft worldwide.

name: Kepler Communications
short_description: Runs a data-relay constellation connecting satellites in low Earth orbit.
why_relevant: Creates the data highways that let satellites talk to Earth once a day.
history: Founded in 2015 in Toronto, Kepler Communications is building a data-relay constellation to connect satellites in low Earth orbit. After launching early demonstration satellites, it raised more than $200 million and moved toward optical inter-satellite links. Its network aims to give spacecraft continuous connectivity rather than brief ground-station passes. Kepler serves government and commercial customers and is a key player in Canada's space sector.

name: ICEYE
short_description: Synthetic-aperture radar satellites that see through clouds day and night.
why_relevant: Radar imaging market leader for insurance and maritime surveillance.
history: Founded in 2014 in Espoo, Finland, ICEYE built the world's first small synthetic-aperture radar satellite, launched in 2018. Its MicroSAR constellation provides all-weather, day-night imaging used for flood, maritime, and insurance analytics. ICEYE raised hundreds of millions and expanded into defense and data services. From its Finnish headquarters, it leads the commercial SAR market with rapid revisit and interferometric capabilities.

name: Capella Space
short_description: High-frequency SAR satellite tasking for defense and intelligence.
why_relevant: Rapid revisit SAR that supports day-and-night surveillance anywhere.
history: Founded in 2016, Capella Space operates X-band SAR satellites delivering high-resolution imagery regardless of weather or light. Its first satellite launched in 2018, and the company expanded to a constellation offering rapid tasking for defense and intelligence customers. Backed by venture funding and headquartered in San Francisco, Capella pioneered automated SAR tasking, letting clients request and receive radar images of any location within hours.

name: Astroscale
short_description: Removes space debris and services satellites in orbit.
why_relevant: First commercial demonstration of docking to and de-orbiting junk.
history: Founded in 2013 in Tokyo, Astroscale became the first company to demonstrate commercial rendezvous and docking with orbital debris. Its ELSA-d mission in 2021 proved magnetic capture technology, and follow-on programs target end-of-life servicing and debris removal. Active across Japan, the United Kingdom, and the United States, Astroscale works with space agencies to establish a sustainable on-orbit servicing economy and has raised substantial funding.

name: Pixxel
short_description: Deploys hyperspectral satellites to map the chemical fingerprint of the Earth.
why_relevant: Demonstrates how spectral data can detect spills, crops and minerals.
history: Founded in 2019 in Bengaluru, Pixxel develops hyperspectral satellites that capture hundreds of spectral bands to identify materials, crops, and pollution from orbit. After raising tens of millions and launching demonstration spacecraft, its Firefly constellation began commercial imaging. The company partners with agriculture, mining, and defense clients, positioning India as a leader in advanced Earth observation and spectral analytics.

name: Satellogic
short_description: High-resolution sub-meter imaging constellation from Latin America.
why_relevant: Latin America's champion in commercial high-resolution EO.
history: Founded in 2010 in Buenos Aires, Satellogic builds low-cost sub-meter Earth-observation satellites through vertical integration. It launched its first spacecraft in 2013, went public via a SPAC in 2022, and operates the Aleph constellation for high-frequency imaging. Serving government and commercial customers worldwide, Satellogic champions affordable, Latin American-led access to geospatial data and analytics.

name: Umbra
short_description: High-resolution SAR with frequent revisits from a smaller sensor.
why_relevant: Defense and climate clients buy quick, affordable radar change detection.
history: Founded in 2015 in Santa Barbara, Umbra develops compact X-band SAR satellites delivering high-resolution radar imagery. Its first satellite launched in 2021, and the company offers rapid tasking with frequent revisits for defense and climate customers. Funded by venture capital and defense contracts, Umbra provides affordable change detection and all-weather monitoring from a growing constellation of small radar spacecraft.

name: Loft Orbital
short_description: Rideshare operator that flies customer payloads on a standardized satellite bus.
why_relevant: Turns space missions into the simplicity of renting a server.
history: Founded in 2017, Loft Orbital operates standardized satellite buses, its YAM series, that host multiple customer payloads on rideshare launches. This space-infrastructure-as-a-service model lets clients fly missions without building their own spacecraft. With offices in San Francisco, Denver, and France, Loft has launched several missions and raised significant funding to simplify and accelerate access to orbit.

name: Vyoma
short_description: Tracks space debris with optical sensors and provides early collision warnings.
why_relevant: Protects low-Earth orbit value from a growing debris population.
history: Founded in 2020 in Munich, Vyoma builds an optical sensor network and software to track space debris and predict collisions. Its ground-based telescopes monitor objects in low Earth orbit, feeding a data platform that warns satellite operators of close approaches. As debris concerns grow, Vyoma provides space situational awareness services to commercial and government clients across Europe.

name: Sierra Space
short_description: Developer of the Dream Chaser spaceplane and inflatable station modules.
why_relevant: NASA-certified cargo spaceplane path to a commercial LEO economy.
history: Founded in 2021 as a spin-off of Sierra Nevada Corporation, Sierra Space develops the Dream Chaser spaceplane for NASA cargo resupply and the inflatable LIFE habitat for commercial stations. Dream Chaser completed key tests toward its first ISS mission. Backed by major investment and based in Louisville, Colorado, Sierra Space is central to plans for a commercial low Earth orbit economy.

name: Isar Aerospace
short_description: Builds the Spectrum rocket for dedicated small-satellite launches.
why_relevant: Europe's privately funded answer for sovereign small launch.
history: Founded in 2018 in Munich, Isar Aerospace develops the Spectrum rocket, a two-stage launcher powered by LOX-propane engines for dedicated small-satellite missions. The company raised over $400 million, one of Europe's largest space rounds, and conducted early flight tests from Norway. Isar aims to provide sovereign European launch capacity and competes for institutional and commercial small-launch contracts.

name: Rocket Factory Augsburg
short_description: Develops the RFA One rocket and first gained Europe's offshore launch permit.
why_relevant: Serial-production launch concept designed for hundreds of flights a year.
history: Founded in 2018 in Augsburg, Rocket Factory Augsburg develops the RFA One rocket using serial production and staged-combustion engines. It secured Europe's first offshore launch permit and progressed through integrated engine tests, though a 2024 static-fire anomaly destroyed a first stage. Backed by OHB and private investors, RFA targets high-cadence, low-cost European launch for small satellites.

name: Skyroot Aerospace
short_description: First Indian private rocket company to reach space with Vikram.
why_relevant: Opened the commercial small-launch market in India.
history: Founded in 2018 in Hyderabad, Skyroot Aerospace became the first Indian private company to reach space when its Vikram-S rocket flew in 2022. Using carbon-composite structures and 3D-printed engines, it develops the Vikram family for small-satellite launch. Backed by major Indian investors, Skyroot has opened India's commercial launch market and supports the country's private space ambitions.

name: Agnikul Cosmos
short_description: Develops the Agnibaan rocket with 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engines.
why_relevant: India's first private singularity launch with a fully 3D-printed engine.
history: Founded in 2017 in Chennai, Agnikul Cosmos develops the Agnibaan rocket, featuring a fully 3D-printed, single-piece semi-cryogenic engine. In 2024 it conducted India's first private suborbital launch from Sriharikota. Backed by venture funding and supported by ISRO, Agnikul focuses on on-demand small-satellite launch with a simplified, rapidly manufacturable vehicle.

name: PLD Space
short_description: Made Europe's first private rocket launch, the Miura 1, then Miura 5.
why_relevant: Southern Europe's sovereign access to orbit through recoverable rockets.
history: Founded in 2011 in Elche, Spain, PLD Space became the first private European company to launch a rocket when Miura 1 flew suborbitally in 2023. The company is now developing the larger, partially reusable Miura 5 for orbital missions. Backed by Spanish and European investors, PLD Space aims to give southern Europe sovereign, recoverable access to space for small payloads.

name: Momentus
short_description: Provides in-space transport and tug services to arbitrary orbits.
why_relevant: Transports small satellites to precision orbits after rideshare.
history: Founded in 2017 in San Jose, Momentus provides orbital transfer vehicles and in-space transportation using water-based propulsion. It went public in 2021 but faced technical and financial difficulties, later pivoting and restructuring. Its Vigoride tugs have flown several missions, aiming to deliver small satellites to precise orbits after rideshare launches, though the company has since scaled back operations.

name: The Exploration Company
short_description: Develops Nyx, a reusable orbital capsule for cargo and crew.
why_relevant: European modular capsule serving commercial LEO stations.
history: Founded in 2021, The Exploration Company develops Nyx, a reusable orbital capsule for cargo and eventually crew, serving commercial space stations. With teams in Bordeaux and Munich, it won ESA and commercial contracts and raised substantial venture funding. Nyx is designed to be modular and refuelable, positioning the Franco-German startup as a European counterpart to SpaceX's Dragon.

name: Axiom Space
short_description: Files private astronaut missions and builds commercial space stations.
why_relevant: First commercial modules slated to dock to the ISS then detach as a station.
history: Founded in 2016 in Houston, Axiom Space flies private astronaut missions to the International Space Station and is building a commercial station. It conducted the first all-private ISS mission in 2022 and holds NASA contracts for station modules that will eventually detach to form an independent outpost. Backed by major investment, Axiom leads the commercialization of low Earth orbit.

name: Vast
short_description: Builds the Haven private space station, the first commercial VLEO habitat.
why_relevant: Plans the first all-commercial crewed station earlier than incumbents.
history: Founded in 2021, Vast is developing the Haven commercial space station, aiming for the first privately built crewed habitat in low Earth orbit. It has launched precursor missions and secured SpaceX flights, targeting earlier crewed operations than many competitors. Backed by billionaire Jed McCaleb and based in Long Beach, California, Vast pursues artificial-gravity concepts and a private LEO destination.

name: Sidus Space
short_description: Builds LizzieSat buses for on-demand missions including defense.
why_relevant: Quirky standardized bus that lets anyone fly a payload fast.
history: Founded in 2012 in Cape Canaveral, Florida, Sidus Space builds the LizzieSat small satellite bus for on-demand, multi-mission payloads including defense applications. The company went public in 2021 and has launched LizzieSat spacecraft featuring 3D-printed components and AI-enabled edge processing. Sidus offers end-to-end satellite manufacturing and data services, positioning itself as a flexible provider for government and commercial customers.

name: AstroForge
short_description: Aims to refine metals in space and bring them back to Earth.
why_relevant: First private company to put a tanker prototype into orbit for asteroid mining.
history: Founded in 2022, AstroForge aims to mine and refine platinum-group metals from asteroids. It launched a demonstration spacecraft in 2023 and is developing technology for in-space refining to avoid returning heavy ore to Earth. Backed by venture capital and headquartered in Huntington Beach, California, AstroForge pursues a long-term vision of off-world resource extraction despite significant technical and economic hurdles.

name: K2 Space
short_description: Builds large standard buses for mega satellites and constellations.
why_relevant: Low-cost high-power buses sized for the next API generation of satellites.
history: Founded in 2022, K2 Space builds large, high-power satellite buses intended to lower the cost of mega-constellations and demanding national security missions. The company raised one of the sector's largest early rounds and is developing spacecraft far larger than typical smallsats. Based in Torrance, California, K2 Space aims to supply the next generation of high-capability satellites at mass-production prices.

name: Impulse Space
short_description: Builds the Helios and Mira orbital tugs for in-space transport.
why_relevant: High-ΔV tugs promise same-day inter-orbit rideshare deliveries.
history: Founded in 2021 by former SpaceX propulsion lead Tom Mueller, Impulse Space develops the Mira and Helios orbital transfer vehicles for in-space transportation. Its cryogenic tugs aim to move satellites to precise orbits after rideshare launches, with high-ΔV missions planned. Backed by significant venture funding and based in Redondo Beach, California, Impulse targets fast, flexible orbital logistics.

name: Terran Orbital
short_description: Designs and manufactures smallsats for defense constellations.
why_relevant: Key manufacturing partner for large US defense constellations.
history: Founded in 2013, Terran Orbital designs and manufactures small satellites for large defense constellations, notably supporting Lockheed Martin's programs. It went public in 2022 and built a high-volume factory in Florida, though it faced financial losses. In 2024 Lockheed Martin acquired the company, securing a key US smallsat manufacturing capability from its Boca Raton, Florida base.
